ads_ratio.reason: QIAGEN is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded QGEN share is one common share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-20), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) of the Act are 'Common Shares, par value EUR 0.01 per share', trading symbol QGEN, name of exchange: New York Stock Exchange — the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS

moat_against: Revenue stalled: 3-yr revenue CAGR -0.8%; FY2026 outlook reaffirmed at +1-2% CER sales growth
ROIC proxy only ~7-12% in clean years — returns do not compound at wide-moat rates
Crowded field: Thermo Fisher, Roche, Danaher/Cepheid and bioMérieux contest every platform category
QuantiFERON hit by the decline in U.S. immigration testing demand; China sales down low-teens in 2026
NeuMoDx failure (~$400M pre-tax discontinuation charge in 2024) shows platform bets can miss; goodwill is 44.7% of assets
moat_for: QuantiFERON-TB: dominant latent-TB test franchise with automated-workflow lock-in
Sample technologies leadership: large installed instrument base pulling recurring consumables
QIAstat-Dx installed base of more than 5,200 cumulative placements in 100+ countries (end of 2025, company release) with an expanding FDA-cleared menu
QIAGEN Digital Insights bioinformatics: data/software with recurring revenue
Gross margin 62-65% in clean years (2021-2023, 2025) on a consumables-heavy mix
moat_justification: Real but narrow franchises: QuantiFERON-TB, Sample technologies and the QIAstat-Dx installed base pull recurring consumables at 62-65% gross margins, but the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is only 12.41% (2021), 9.54% (2022), 7.00% (2023), 1.57% (2024, NeuMoDx charge year), 8.79% (2025) — above the cost of capital in clean years, not at wide-moat rates — and revenue has stalled (3-yr revenue CAGR -0.8%, FY2026 guided +1-2% CER). Moderate/narrow moat, 5/10.
